symbols: cross-price elasticity of X with respect to price of Y
percentage change in demand for X
percentage change in price of Y
Income and cross-price elasticity.example: At Y=₹20,000, Q=50 and dQ/dY=0.005, income elasticity is 2. If Y’s price rises 10% and demand for X rises 5%, cross-price elasticity is 0.5.

Price, MR and elasticity.example: For P=₹100 and Eₚ=−2, MR=₹50 per item.

symbols: amount of Y surrendered for one more X on an indifference curve
Budget line and marginal rate of substit.example: At Pₓ=₹20, Pᵧ=₹10 and M=₹100, (3,4) costs ₹100. If getting 1 more X on an indifference curve costs 2 units of Y, MRS is 2.

symbols: price received by the seller before tax
ad valorem tax as a decimal of seller price
Per-unit and ad valorem tax.example: A seller price of ₹100 with a 12% tax gives P꜀=₹112. A ₹12 per-unit tax gives the same wedge at this price.

symbols: average output per unit of labour
marginal output per additional unit of labour
Average and marginal product.example: Q=100 and L=5 gives AP=20 items per labour unit. If one extra labour unit increases output by about 12 items, MP is about 12.

Isoquant–isocost tangency.example: If MPₗ=12, MPₖ=6, w=₹200 and r=₹100, both ratios equal 2 at the candidate tangency.

symbols: sum of the labour and capital exponents
Cobb–Douglas scale.example: With exponents 0.6 and 0.4, doubling both inputs doubles output because 2¹=2.

Cost identities.example: For TC=₹700, TVC=₹500 and Q=100, AC=₹7 and AVC=₹5 per item. If one extra item adds about ₹4 in cost, MC is about ₹4 per item.

Average-cost turning point.example: At Q=100, MC=₹5 and AC=₹7, the derivative is −0.02, so AC is falling.

symbols: average variable cost when labour is the only variable input
Cost–product links.example: At w=₹100, APₗ=20 and MPₗ=10, AVC=₹5 and MC=₹10 per item.

Contribution and P/V ratio.example: With p=₹50 and v=₹30, c=₹20 and P/V=40%.

symbols: sales volume for the target profit
Break-even and target units.example: With FC=₹1,000, c=₹20, and target profit ₹400, break-even is 50 units and the target is 70.

symbols: break-even sales on the same basis
Margin of safety.example: Actual sales of ₹12,000 and break-even sales of ₹9,000 give a margin of ₹3,000.

symbols: number of compounding periods per year

Single-sum equivalence.example: ₹1,000 at 10% per year for two years grows to ₹1,210.

symbols: future worth factor for unit end-of-period payments
present worth factor for unit end-of-period payments
negative payment count in the discount exponent
Ordinary annuity.example: At i=10%, two year-end payments of ₹100 have FW=₹210 and PW≈₹173.55.

symbols: uniform annuity per unit arithmetic gradient
number of periods in the exponent
Arithmetic gradient.example: At 10% over two years, A/G≈0.47619. Cash flows ₹0 then ₹100 are equivalent to two ₹47.62 payments.

symbols: net cash flow in period t
Present, future and annual worth.example: A ₹121 receipt at year 2 with i=10% has PW=₹100 and FW=₹121. Since the two-year P/A factor is about 1.7355, AW is about ₹57.62 per year.

symbols: ratio of discounted benefits to discounted costs
discounted benefit streams in the numerator
discounted cost streams in the denominator
Benefit–cost ratio.example: ₹150 lakh in present benefits divided by ₹100 lakh in present costs gives B/C=1.5.

symbols: net present value at the specified discount rate
time to recover the initial investment without discounting
investment still unrecovered at that point
cash inflow during the recovery year
IRR and payback.example: Investing ₹100 today for ₹110 one year later gives IRR=10%. An unrecovered ₹30 with ₹60 expected uniformly next year adds 0.5 years to payback.

symbols: depreciation in year t under sum-of-years’ digits
Straight line and SYD.example: For P=₹1,000, S=₹100 and n=3, straight line gives ₹300 a year and first-year SYD gives ₹450.

symbols: future worth factor for annual deposits
book value at the end of year t
Sinking fund.example: With P=₹1,000, S=₹100, i=10% and n=2, D≈₹428.57. End-of-year-one book value is about ₹571.43.

symbols: book value at the start of the year
Declining balance.example: At opening BV ₹110, r=20% and S=₹100, depreciation is min(₹22,₹10)=₹10.
